span.label: mechanism
span.quote: One important contribution of our research relates to its specification and testing of a mediating mechanism—the current accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept—through which situational factors and moral identity centrality influence moral intentions and behaviors.

span.label: moral identity accessibility and moral behavior
span.quote: This article proposes and tests a social-cognitive framework for examining the joint influence of situational factors and the centrality of moral identity on moral intentions and behaviors.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: A two-group design with a control condition and a moral prime condition was used in the in-lab priming experiment.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: moral behavior depends on the situational accessibility of moral identity: cues that make moral identity salient in the working self-concept increase moral motivation, while cues that suppress it (e.g. money/material primes) reduce moral behavior
span.quote: if a situational factor increases the current accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept, then it strengthens the motivation to act morally

span.label: Only a small number of situational factors were examined, out of an unknown and multifarious range.
span.quote: First, only a small number of specific situational factors were examined in our studies.

span.label: Neither moral prime used (Ten Commandments recall, handwriting task) has practical utility for actually promoting moral action outside the lab.
span.quote: For those who may be interested in promoting moral action, the limited number of situations we studied is particularly lamentable because neither of the moral primes used in our studies (i.e., recalling and reading a list of the Ten Commandments and completing a handwriting task) would seem to have practical utility.

span.label: The posited dissonant psychological tension that is supposed to drive the deactivation of moral identity was never directly measured.
span.quote: Although there is ample evidence to support our rationale (cf. Burroughs & Rindfleisch, 2002; Kasser et al., 2007), the direct assessment of aroused psychological tensions resulting from self-interest-promoting situational factors would further increase confidence in the veracity of this explanation.

span.label: The studies do not address the psychological or emotional aftermath for high-centrality participants who were induced to behave selfishly.
span.quote: One interesting question that our studies do not address is what happens when people with highly central moral identities behave in a selfish fashion (as they were induced to do by self-interest-promoting situational cues in Studies 3 and 4).

span.label: Studies 1 and 2 measured behavioral intentions rather than actual behavior (Study 3 was run to address this).
span.quote: However, in both studies we examined behavioral intentions rather than actual behaviors.

span.label: Study 3 did not measure the proposed mediator; deactivation of moral identity there is inferred from Study 2 rather than observed.
span.quote: However, in Study 3 we did not measure the current accessibility of moral identity but rely on the findings from Study 2 to infer that deactivation of moral identity is responsible for any observed increase in lying.

span.label: The cumulative-experience explanation offered for why some people show enduring and others variable moral commitment is not rigorously tested by the data.
span.quote: Although our studies do not provide a rigorous test of this cumulative experiences-based explanation for predicting enduring versus variable commitment to moral action, findings from Study 4 are consistent with this rationale.

span.label: The predicted three-way interaction with reward size ($50 vs $150) in Study 3 was not supported.
span.quote: We did not find support for the hypothesized three-way interaction involving moral identity, incentives, and reward size.

span.label: a minimal-difference control condition: the ONLY thing that differed was the general knowledge items
span.note: eliminates: that anything else in the procedure - length, difficulty, instructions - produced the effect attributed to the moral prime
span.quote: Moral Priming Manipulation The only difference between the control condition and the moral prime condition involved the general knowledge items.

span.quote: The observation that the current accessibility of moral identity mediated the interactive influence of the moral prime and the centrality of moral identity on intentions to behave morally supports this notion

span.label: current accessibility
span.quote: The observation that the current accessibility of moral identity mediated the interactive influence of the moral prime and the centrality of moral identity on intentions to behave morally supports this notion

span.quote: the prime is expected to activate an otherwise dormant aspect of the self-concept for people low in moral identity centrality but have little influence on people with highly central moral identities because their moral self-schemas are already accessible

span.label: activation potential
span.quote: Activation potential refers to the extent to which a knowledge structure tends to be readily accessible for processing and acting on information

span.label: working self-concept
span.quote: the current accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept links situational factors and moral identity centrality to moral action. Study 1 showed that priming people to activate moral constructs

span.label: moral action
span.quote: the current accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept links situational factors and moral identity centrality to moral action. Study 1 showed that priming people to activate moral constructs

span.label: **THE PRIME WORKS LEAST ON THE PEOPLE IT IS ABOUT, AND THIS IS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE RATHER THAN EXPLAINED AFTERWARDS:** `the prime is expected to activate an otherwise DORMANT aspect of the self-concept for people LOW in moral identity centrality but HAVE LITTLE INFLUENCE on people with highly central moral identities BECAUSE THEIR MORAL SELF-SCHEMAS ARE ALREADY ACCESSIBLE.` higgins1977 raises exactly this variable in ONE CONJECTURAL SENTENCE - `There may even be individual differences in the relative accessibility of different categories` - and does not test it. **This paper builds four studies on it and finds it REVERSES the priming effect**, so the same trait that makes someone morally consistent is the one that makes them unprimeable. A 1977 aside and its test 32 years later, both in this corpus. (The term `chronic accessibility` is Higgins, King & Mavin 1982 and appears nowhere in higgins1977.) A study sampling only committed people would find nothing and conclude the effect is not real
span.quote: In other words, the prime is expected to activate an otherwise dormant aspect of the self-concept for people low in moral identity centrality but have little influence on people with highly central moral identities because their moral self-schemas are already accessible

span.label: **PRIMING PLACED AS ONE ROUTE AMONG THREE TO THE SAME STATE:** `The activation potential of any particular knowledge structure can be the result of several factors ranging from FREQUENT PRIMING, to INHERITED PERSONALITY ORIENTATIONS, to REPEATED ACTS OF self-definition (Higgins, 1989).` Three roads to accessibility, of which the experimental one is only the fastest. **That sentence does more for a corpus about priming than most results do, because it says what priming is an INSTANCE OF** - and it makes the individual-difference moderator in this paper a consequence of the theory rather than a nuisance variable. (The quote stops before `self-definition`, which the staged text renders as a hyphen-loss fusion.)
span.quote: The activation potential of any particular knowledge structure can be the result of several factors ranging from frequent priming, to inherited personality orientations

span.label: **AND STUDY 4 REVERSES THE MODERATION OVER TIME, WHICH A ONE-SHOT STUDY WOULD HAVE SCORED AS A NULL:** initially the prime does little for high-centrality people, exactly as the ceiling account predicts. But under repeated feedback that others are behaving selfishly, `WITHOUT A MORAL PRIME, participants for whom moral identity was highly central DID NOT SUSTAIN an increased level of cooperative behavior in the face of selfish behavior by others.` **The prime's value is not the initial push but the resistance to decay.** A corpus that records only peak effect sizes cannot represent this finding at all
span.quote: Without a moral prime, participants for whom moral identity was highly central did not sustain an increased level of cooperative behavior in the face of selfish behavior by others

span.label: **THE MODERATION IS STATED TWICE AND THE SECOND TIME IT IS A RESULT:** `However, the influence of moral priming IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS PEOPLE. Rather, moral priming appears to have STRONGER effects on people for whom moral identity has relatively LOW centrality because such priming has GREATER POTENTIAL to increase the accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept.` The mechanism is a headroom argument, and it is testable: it predicts that any manipulation raising a construct's accessibility will show the same inverse relation to that construct's chronic strength. **This record and higgins1977 are the two ends of that claim in this corpus, and the two ends are not equal** - higgins1977 says only `THERE MAY EVEN BE individual differences in the relative accessibility of different categories`, a speculation with no test attached, while this paper makes that variable its moderator and predicts where a prime will fail
span.quote: However, the influence of moral priming is not uniform across people. Rather, moral priming appears to have stronger effects on people for whom moral identity has relatively low centrality because such priming has greater potential to increase the accessibility of moral identity within the working self-concept

span.label: builds-on → social-cognitive theory (Bandura, 2001)
span.quote: Our theoretical framework is grounded in social-cognitive theory (Bandura, 2001) and uses concepts and psychological mechanisms from social cognition to offer specific predictions about when and how the influence of situational factors on moral behaviors will be moderated by the centrality of moral identity.

span.label: builds-on → Aquino and Reed's (2002) moral identity Internalization measure
span.quote: The Internalization subscale of Aquino and Reed’s (2002) moral identity measure was used to assess centrality in all studies reported herein.

span.label: builds-on → Muller, Judd, and Yzerbyt's (2005) mediated moderation procedure
span.quote: Therefore, the present analysis followed established prescriptions for testing mediated moderation hypotheses (see Muller, Judd, & Yzerbyt, 2005).

span.label: extends → Walker and Frimer (2007), whose call for systematic exploration of person-situation interaction in the moral domain the framework answers
span.quote: In response to their plea, we propose a theoretical framework that explains how situational factors and a relatively stable individual characteristic that we refer to as the centrality of moral identity (Aquino & Reed, 2002) jointly influence moral behavior.

span.label: contradicts → research conceptualising moral identity as enduring and stable (Blasi; Colby & Damon; Damon & Hart; Walker & Frimer; Walker & Hennig)
span.quote: At first glance, the observation that situational cues can promote self-interested behavior even among people for whom moral identity has high centrality (Studies 3 and 4) appears to contradict a large body of research that conceptualizes moral identity as enduring and stable (cf. Blasi, 1984, 2005; Colby & Damon, 1992, 1993; Damon, 1984; Damon & Hart, 1992; Walker & Frimer, 2007; Walker & Hennig, 2004).

span.label: moral prime —causes→ current accessibility
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **`INTERACTIVE INFLUENCE` IS IN THE QUOTE AND IS THE PART THIS EDGE CANNOT CARRY.** The measured relation is not `prime raises accessibility` but `prime raises accessibility MORE for people low in moral identity centrality, and barely at all for people high in it`. `increases` is true on average and is what the study found; a reader who stops there has the paper's headline and not its result. The moderation is quoted whole in the first and fourth senses. Weight 0.9 - four studies, and the mediation is formally tested by Muller et al.'s procedure rather than asserted.
span.quote: The observation that the current accessibility of moral identity mediated the interactive influence of the moral prime and the centrality of moral identity on intentions to behave morally supports this notion

span.label: current accessibility —causes→ moral action
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE SECOND LEG OF THE MEDIATION, and together with the edge above it is the paper's model written as a path: situation -> current accessibility -> moral action. `LINKS` is the paper's own verb and it is doing mediation work - this is the summary sentence for Studies 1 and 2 in the general discussion, not a hypothesis. Weight 0.9.

span.label: moral identity centrality —causes→ current accessibility
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — **THE TRAIT LEG, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE PAPER'S RESULT COUNTERINTUITIVE.** Centrality raises chronic accessibility - which is why the PRIME does less for people high in it. So this edge and the `moral prime -> current accessibility` edge point at the same target for opposite reasons, and the graph shows two arrows where the paper has a ceiling. **`moderates` is not in the enforced vocabulary (Q-804)**, so nothing here records that the second edge shrinks as the first grows. Weight 0.85 rather than 0.9: this leg is theory plus the Study 1 mediation test, where the prime leg is directly manipulated.
